title: Grouping of Figures
parentNote: This unit is like sorting toys into two baskets. Ask him to name the RULE for each basket before deciding where a new item goes.
learnBullets: Sorting figures/numbers/animals into **two groups** based on a shared rule
Deciding which group a **new item** belongs to
Spotting when something belongs to **both** groups, or to **neither**
learnItFirst:
**The Big Idea:** Look at the figures already sorted into Group 1 and Group 2, figure out the RULE for each group, then use that rule to sort a new figure.

```
Group 1: ■  ▬  ⬛     (all have 4 sides)
Group 2: ▲  ◺          (all have 3 sides)

New shape: ◆ (a diamond — it has 4 sides)
→ It goes into Group 1!
```

**Watch out for tricky ones:**
- A new item might fit **both** groups (like the number 10, which is a multiple of both 5 and 10).
- A new item might fit **neither** group (like a 3-digit number when the groups only have 1-digit and 2-digit numbers).

### 🧠 How to Solve — 3 Easy Steps
1. **Name** the rule for Group 1 out loud ("all shapes with 4 sides").
2. **Name** the rule for Group 2 out loud ("all shapes with 3 sides").
3. **Test** the new item against each rule before choosing.

---

questions.content: Which of these belongs to the group of CURVED shapes?
questions.why: A circle is the only one with a curved (round) side

questions.content: Which of these belongs to the group of STRAIGHT-SIDED shapes?
questions.why: A triangle is made only of straight sides

questions.content: Red group: 🔴🔴🔴. Blue group: 🔵🔵. Which group has MORE figures?
questions.why: Red has 3 figures; Blue has only 2

questions.content: Which shape does NOT belong to the "4 sides" group: ■, ▬, ⬛, ▲?
questions.why: A triangle has 3 sides, not 4 like the rest

questions.content: Which animal belongs to the SAME group as 🐦 (2 legs)?
questions.why: A hen has 2 legs, just like a bird

questions.content: Which animal belongs to the SAME group as 🐄 (4 legs)?
questions.why: A goat has 4 legs, just like a cow

questions.content: Small shapes: ▲ ●. Big shapes: ⬤ ■. Which shape belongs with ⬤ (big)?
questions.why: The square is drawn big, matching the big-shapes group

questions.content: Even numbers group: 2, 4. Which number belongs in this group?
questions.why: 6 is an even number, like 2 and 4

questions.content: Odd numbers group: 1, 3, 5. Which number belongs in this group?
questions.why: 7 is an odd number, like 1, 3, and 5

questions.content: Filled (solid) shapes group: ⬛ ▲(filled). Which shape belongs in this group?
questions.why: It is filled/solid, matching the filled-shapes group

questions.content: Group 1 (4 sides): ■ ▬ ⬛. Group 2 (3 sides): ▲. A diamond ◆ (4 sides) belongs to:
questions.why: A diamond has 4 sides, matching Group 1's rule

questions.content: Group 1: colours 🔴🔵🟡. Group 2: outline shapes ▲■●. A new colour 🟢 belongs to:
questions.why: Green is a colour, matching Group 1's rule

questions.content: Group 1 (can roll): ⚽ 🥫. Group 2 (cannot roll): 📦 🎲. A round orange 🍊 belongs to:
questions.why: An orange is round and can roll, matching Group 1's rule

questions.content: Group 1 (even numbers): 2, 4, 6, 8. Group 2 (odd numbers): 1, 3, 5, 7. The number 12 belongs to:
questions.why: 12 is an even number

questions.content: Group 1 (2-legged animals): 🐦 🐔 🦆. Group 2 (4-legged animals): 🐄 🐐 🐎. A swan 🦢 (2 legs) belongs to:
questions.why: A swan has 2 legs, matching Group 1's rule

questions.content: In this set: ▲ ▲ ▲ ■ — how many figures belong to the triangle group?
questions.why: There are three ▲ symbols in the set

questions.content: In this set: ● ● ■ ■ ■ — how many figures belong to the square group?
questions.why: There are three ■ symbols in the set

questions.content: Group 1 (only straight sides): ▲ ■ ▬. Group 2 (has a curve): ● ⬤. A crescent moon 🌙 belongs to:
questions.why: A crescent moon has a curved edge, matching Group 2's rule

questions.content: Group A (multiples of 2): 2, 4, 6, 8. Group B (multiples of 4): 4, 8, 12. The number 8 belongs to:
questions.why: 8 is a multiple of 2 AND a multiple of 4

questions.content: Which shape does NOT belong to the group "shapes with 4 corners": ■, ▬, ⬛, ▲?
questions.why: A triangle has 3 corners, not 4 like the rest

questions.content: Which number does NOT belong to the "multiples of 3" group: 3, 6, 9, 10?
questions.why: 10 is not a multiple of 3 (3, 6, 9 are; 10 is not)

questions.content: Group X (red fruits): 🍎 🍒 🍓. Group Y (yellow fruits): 🍌 🍋. A purple grape 🍇 belongs to:
questions.why: A grape is purple, not red or yellow

questions.content: Group 1 (even number of sides): ■ (4) and ⬡ (6). Group 2 (odd number of sides): ▲ (3) and ⬠ (5). A rectangle ▬ (4 sides) belongs to:
questions.why: A rectangle has 4 sides, which is an even number

questions.content: Sort by number of legs: Table 🪑 (4), Chair 🪑 (4), Bird 🐦 (2), Human 🚶 (2). How many belong to the "2 legs" group?
questions.why: Only the bird and the human have 2 legs

questions.content: Group 1 (looks the same when flipped): ● ■. Group 2 (looks different when flipped): 👣 (footprint). Where does an equal-sided triangle ▲ belong?
questions.why: An equal-sided triangle looks the same after a flip

questions.content: Group 1 (2-digit numbers): 10, 25, 99. Group 2 (1-digit numbers): 1, 5, 9. The number 100 belongs to:
questions.why: 100 has 3 digits, so it fits neither the 1-digit nor 2-digit group

questions.content: Group 1 (odd number of sides): ▲ (3), ⬠ (5). Group 2 (even number of sides): ■ (4), ⬡ (6). A stop-sign shape 🛑 (8 sides) belongs to:
questions.why: 8 is an even number of sides

questions.content: Group A (lay eggs): 🐔 🐦 🐍. Group B (give birth to live babies): 🐄 🐕 🐘. A turtle 🐢 (lays eggs) belongs to:
questions.why: Turtles lay eggs, just like the animals in Group A

questions.content: Group 1 (numbers 1–10): 3, 7. Group 2 (numbers 11–20): 13, 18. The number 25 belongs to:

options.C: Neither — it is bigger than both groups' ranges

questions.why: 25 is greater than 20, so it doesn't fit either range

questions.content: Group 1 (straight sides + 4 corners): ■ ▬. Group 2 (straight sides + 3 corners): ▲. A pentagon ⬠ (5 corners) belongs to:
questions.why: A pentagon has 5 corners, which matches neither the 4-corner nor 3-corner group
